dataNote: Editorial records were checked October 12, 2026. No live measurements are included. Missing readings must remain unavailable. Southwest Washington records were added October 14, 2026 from search excerpts of the listed sources; their rules alerts need a trip-day check.

planning.access_summary: Trout Creek: bank, trail, boat ramp
planning.access_detail: BLM lists day-use parking, a boat launch and an upriver trail at Trout Creek Campground. The approach includes gravel and a narrow tunnel; bring water. This is a public destination on the reach, not directions to the Madras gauge.

access_point.label: Trout Creek Campground
access_point.map_query: BLM Trout Creek Campground Deschutes River Madras Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: Resident redband trout are a core lower-river fishery. Treat seasonal steelhead descriptions as historical run context: current species restrictions take precedence.
planning.methods: ODFW reports stonefly nymphs and evening dry flies for trout; check exact tackle rules.

report.summary: ODFW reports good trout fishing.
report.coverage: Mouth-to-Pelton report; not a Trout Creek catch survey.

alerts.summary: Aug 15-Dec 31, 2026: steelhead and coho angling/retention closed from Sherars Falls to Pelton Reregulating Reservoir. Review Chinook rules separately.
Boater permits, land boundaries and current trail/fire restrictions need a trip-day check.

planning.score_notice: ODFW reports steelhead and salmon restrictions for this reach; the fishing score is withheld pending a rules review.
planning.score_species_note: Trout-only score. Steelhead and coho are restricted on this reach and are not scored.

planning.access_summary: State park: bank and riverside trails
planning.access_detail: Deschutes River State Recreation Area provides a public starting point at the river mouth. Its Blackberry Trail follows the east bank; Heritage Landing is the separate boat launch across the river. The station itself is not the access destination.

access_point.label: Deschutes River State Recreation Area
access_point.map_query: Deschutes River State Recreation Area 89600 Biggs Rufus Highway Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: ODFW describes resident redband trout and a historical summer/fall steelhead run in the lower Deschutes. Run timing does not establish an open fishery; this mouth-area row has a current restriction.
planning.methods: ODFW reports stonefly nymphs for trout. Use permitted bank locations and verify tackle rules.

report.summary: ODFW reports good trout fishing.
report.coverage: Mouth-to-Pelton report; not a Moody-area catch survey.

alerts.summary: Aug 15-Dec 31, 2026: salmon/steelhead angling and retention closed from the westbound I-84 bridge to the trestle three miles below Sherars Falls.
Confirm river-use permits and park notices before boating or taking the longer canyon trail.

planning.score_notice: ODFW reports steelhead and salmon restrictions for this reach; the fishing score is withheld pending a rules review.
planning.score_species_note: Trout-only score. Steelhead and coho are restricted on this reach and are not scored.

planning.access_summary: Steelhead Falls: hike to river upstream
planning.access_detail: BLM describes a roughly half-mile trail from Steelhead Falls Trailhead to the falls, with a short steep section and no drinking water. This middle-river destination is upstream of the Culver station; it does not establish parking or shoreline access at the gauge.

access_point.label: Steelhead Falls Trailhead
access_point.map_query: BLM Steelhead Falls Trailhead River Road Terrebonne Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: ODFW general trout guidance favors spring and fall in moving water. That is species-level context, not a measured seasonal advantage for this canyon or a prediction of conditions at the falls.
planning.methods: General trout approach: examine current breaks behind rocks and deeper pools; use legal flies or lures suited to that water.

report.summary: ODFW reported productive trout fishing near Steelhead Falls.
report.coverage: Broader middle Deschutes; older than the live Culver readings.

alerts.summary: Exact fishing boundaries, trail condition and fire restrictions are not fully reviewed for this trip.

planning.access_detail: The monitoring station and hydro project do not establish a public fishing entrance, parking permission or an easement. No suitable public destination for the canyon below Opal Springs was verified in this review; do not route to the gauge.
planning.seasonal_detail: ODFW fish-passage material documents native fish connectivity in the Crooked basin and bull trout below the project. This is habitat evidence, not a catch-rate record or a basis for importing the Bowman Dam seasonal outlook.
planning.methods: A reach-specific fishing method is not established. First resolve a legal public access location and exact section rules; then assess the actual bank, current and habitat.

report.summary: No dated fishing report specific to the canyon below Opal Springs was found.
report.coverage: ODFW passage evidence; the Bowman Dam fishing report does not assess this canyon.

alerts.summary: Public access and exact reach rules remain unresolved; a live flow reading does not establish permission to fish.
ODFW documents bull trout below the hydro project; species identification and current protections matter here.

planning.access_detail: No verified public trailhead or launch serving the lower river near the Grandview gauge was established. Camp Sherman and Wizard Falls descriptions concern a different section and are not substituted as access to this row.
planning.seasonal_detail: The broader Metolius fishery has resident trout and a winter bull-trout fishery in ODFW background material. There is no Grandview-specific seasonal assessment, route inspection or abundance estimate in this record.
planning.methods: Broader-river guidance mentions stonefly and midge nymphs. A Grandview-specific presentation or depth is unverified.

report.summary: ODFW reports trout fishing and spawning activity.
report.coverage: Whole-river context, not a Grandview observation.

alerts.summary: Avoid spawning fish and redds; ODFW flags Metolius spawning activity.
Confirm lower-river public access and precise section/tribal boundaries before choosing a route.

waters.name: Crooked River
waters.reach: Bowman Dam to Castle Rock Campground
waters.description: A Central Oregon trout reach downstream of Bowman Dam.

planning.access_summary: Castle Rock: bank access from campground
planning.access_detail: BLM identifies Castle Rock Campground on Highway 27 south of Prineville as a Crooked River access site. It provides an evidenced starting point at the lower end of this Bowman-to-Castle Rock row; verify individual pullouts before parking elsewhere.

access_point.label: Castle Rock Campground
access_point.map_query: BLM Castle Rock Campground Crooked River Highway 27 Prineville Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: ODFW guide timing favors September through mid-May below Bowman. The naturally colored water is not automatically poor fishing; slippery footing deserves a separate on-site assessment.
planning.methods: Small midge, scud and mayfly nymphs feature in ODFW guidance; watch for rising fish.

report.summary: ODFW reports strong trout/whitefish fishing and reduced autumn flows.
report.coverage: Bowman tailwater; not the Opal Springs canyon.

alerts.summary: Autumn storage reduces tailwater flow; assess current conditions before entering the river.
Current wading depth, footing and each roadside access point remain unassessed.

waters.name: Fall River
waters.description: A clear-water trout stream near Sunriver and the Fall River Hatchery.

planning.access_detail: Fall River Hatchery at 15055 S. Century Drive is an official fishing destination. ODFW describes bank access without requiring wading. Use the hatchery-side river access, respecting posted operating areas and visitor hours.

access_point.label: Fall River Hatchery
access_point.map_query: Fall River Hatchery 15055 South Century Drive Bend Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: The guide highlights late-day summer fishing around the hatchery. Seasonal stocking background is not confirmation of a new release today.
planning.methods: Dry flies and nymphs are the guide starting points; choose flies based on insects observed at the water.

report.summary: ODFW reports consistent fly fishing.
report.coverage: Fall River; this profile covers the hatchery area above the falls.

alerts.summary: Barbless flies only. The below-falls seasonal closure concerns a different section.

sources.label: ODFW hatchery location and visitor information

waters.name: Haystack Reservoir
waters.description: A small reservoir near Culver with trout and warmwater species.

planning.access_summary: West Shore: bank, ramp and day use
planning.access_detail: Crook County Parks identifies the West Shore day-use area, boat ramp, boarding floats and trailer parking at 9900 SW Haystack Drive. Irrigation changes the lake level; a listed ramp does not guarantee enough water for a particular boat.

access_point.label: Haystack West Shore Day Use
access_point.map_query: Haystack West Shore Day Use 9900 SW Haystack Drive Culver Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: General ODFW guidance for trout in lakes favors cooler spring/fall water and deeper summer habitat. This is a species pattern, not a measured temperature or Haystack-specific catch forecast.
planning.methods: General trout methods include a retrieved spinner or suspended bait where permitted. Match depth to conditions; no current productive depth is documented for West Shore.

report.summary: ODFW confirms spring stocking; no newer water-specific update.
report.coverage: Reservoir-wide; not a recent West Shore catch report.

alerts.summary: Park operator noted algae buildup on July 16, 2026; this older notice does not describe conditions today.
West ramp usability depends on reservoir level; check the operator before trailering a boat.
Statewide OHA mercury advice applies to bass; review meal guidance before keeping fish.

waters.name: Lake Billy Chinook
waters.reach: Crooked River arm at Cove Palisades
waters.description: Cove Palisades provides a starting point for this canyon reservoir.

planning.access_summary: Crooked River day use: ramp and kayak launch
planning.access_detail: Cove Palisades identifies a boat ramp and accessible kayak launch at Crooked River Day-use Area. Drive to day use rather than assuming the campground is on the shoreline; the connecting road is steep. Winter low water can affect ramps.

access_point.label: Crooked River Day-use Area
access_point.map_query: Crooked River Day Use Area Cove Palisades State Park Culver Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: ODFW kokanee guidance highlights April-August effort and movement to spawning habitat in fall. This general pattern does not locate fish in the Crooked arm or predict a productive depth.
planning.methods: For kokanee, search for schools from a boat and troll or jig at their depth. Bank plans should focus on documented shoreline species rather than assume kokanee are within casting range.

report.summary: ODFW reports lake-wide kokanee catches; Crooked-arm success is unconfirmed.
report.coverage: Lake-wide and Metolius-arm information; not a Crooked-arm sample.

alerts.summary: Statewide OHA mercury advice applies to bass; review meal guidance before keeping fish.
OHA downgraded a bloom advisory on June 29, 2026; consult the current map for the latest status, especially for pets.
Sep 28 park notice closes some camp loops and Lower Deschutes day use; those are separate from this Crooked River day-use destination.
Current bloom extent and exact Crooked-arm fishing rules still need a trip-day review.

waters.name: Columbia River
waters.description: A Portland-area starting point for Columbia River fisheries.

planning.access_detail: Chinook Landing Marine Park in Fairview has six launch lanes, paved parking and restrooms. Metro lists a parking fee. Check ramp operations before towing a boat; a launch is not a verified bank-fishing spot.

access_point.label: Chinook Landing Marine Park
access_point.map_query: Chinook Landing Marine Park 5201 NE 223rd Avenue Fairview Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: Spring Chinook and autumn salmon are distinct planning windows. Run timing and in-season decisions matter more than a fixed best-month label; confirm the fishery and reach before choosing a trip.
planning.methods: ODFW describes trolling flashers and bait or fishing lures from an anchored boat for spring Chinook. This is general technique background, not a current gear or retention authorization.

report.summary: Troutdale checks: 139 boats (272 anglers) kept 54 coho and 12 jacks; 74 Chinook and 27 jacks were released.
report.coverage: ODFW weekly catch checks for the Troutdale reporting area, broader than Chinook Landing. No lower-river walleye or sturgeon checks were reported.

alerts.summary: ODFW lists two adult coho a day, hatchery or wild, upstream of Warrior Rock through Oct 15, then hatchery coho only from Oct 16 to 31. Chinook and steelhead must be released. Confirm in-season changes.
OHA consumption guidance applies to lower Columbia sturgeon. Read the advisory before planning to eat a catch; retention permission is separate.
Local bloom conditions are unverified. Check current notices; an absent advisory does not establish safety.

waters.name: Rogue River
waters.description: An upper Rogue fishing area near Central Point and Denman Wildlife Area.

planning.access_detail: Use TouVelle State Recreation Site at Table Rock Road. The boat ramp is across the bridge from the main picnic area; both sides have facilities. State Parks identifies swift currents and submerged obstructions. Parking permit required.

access_point.label: TouVelle State Recreation Site
access_point.map_query: TouVelle State Recreation Site Table Rock Road Central Point Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: Winter and early spring bring winter steelhead; summer-run fish follow later. These are basin-wide patterns, not a TouVelle catch forecast.
planning.methods: Swing flies or drift nymphs for steelhead, subject to current upper Rogue seasonal gear rules.

report.summary: Upper Rogue update records steelhead and Chinook activity. Hatchery returns and reservoir-release readings are upstream context, not TouVelle observations.
report.coverage: Upper Rogue region; no TouVelle-only catch rate, temperature or flow was provided.

alerts.summary: TouVelle conditions and temporary park notices are unverified. Recheck park access before traveling.
Upper Rogue seasonal gear restrictions need an exact-section review.

waters.name: Umpqua River
waters.reach: Mainstem at Alfred S. Tyson Park, Elkton
waters.description: A mainstem Umpqua location with both warmwater fish and migratory salmonids in ODFW’s guide.

planning.access_detail: ODFW lists a boat ramp and bank fishing at Alfred S. Tyson Park beside the RV park in Elkton. Navigate to the public ramp via River Road. Current ramp usability and shoreline footing have not been inspected.

access_point.label: Alfred S. Tyson Park / Elkton Boat Ramp
access_point.map_query: Alfred S Tyson Park Elkton Boat Ramp River Road Elkton Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: Smallmouth provide a resident fishery alongside migratory salmon, steelhead and shad. ODFW identifies the lower Umpqua as a bass destination; recent mainstem reporting is useful context but does not establish a bite at Elkton.
planning.methods: For smallmouth, work small fish or crayfish imitations with spinning tackle: jigs and spinners are ODFW starting points. Seasonal salmon methods and rules require a separate check.

report.summary: Mainstem bass fishing was fair. Salmon catches described near Reedsport are downstream of this Elkton profile.
report.coverage: Mainstem Umpqua; the salmon observations are at Reedsport, not Alfred S. Tyson Park.

alerts.summary: Permanent cyanobacteria recreational advisory includes the mainstem past Elkton to Sawyers Rapids. Shoreline bedrock pools can contain harmful blooms.
OHA statewide mercury advisory applies to bass. Review species-specific consumption guidance before keeping fish.

waters.name: McKenzie River
waters.description: A middle McKenzie access area downstream of Leaburg Dam.

planning.access_detail: Leaburg Landing is on the McKenzie below Leaburg Dam, not Leaburg Lake. ODFW describes a launch, restrooms and some bank access. Check the exact dam, fish-screen and powerhouse boundaries before fishing.

access_point.label: Leaburg Landing
access_point.map_query: Leaburg Landing McKenzie River Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: ODFW places McKenzie summer steelhead broadly in May-November. Hatchery trout releases provide additional context, without guaranteeing fish at this landing.
planning.methods: Swing flies or drift an indicator nymph for steelhead. Check seasonal gear restrictions before selecting tackle.

report.summary: Below-Leaburg trout stocking ended in the week of Sept. 1, per ODFW.
report.coverage: Below Leaburg Lake; no landing-specific survey or measurement.

alerts.summary: Reach access and temporary restrictions are unverified. Dam, fish-screen and powerhouse closures require an exact-boundary rules check.

waters.name: Willamette River
waters.reach: Cathedral Park at St. Johns Bridge
waters.description: A lower Willamette fishing location in Portland.

planning.access_detail: Portland permits fishing from Cathedral Park riverbank and its upstream fishing/light-watercraft pier. This does not authorize fishing from every dock. The park also has a boat ramp; follow posted uses and parking rules.

access_point.label: Cathedral Park
access_point.map_query: Cathedral Park North Edison Street and Pittsburg Avenue Portland Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: Resident bass and panfish offer a different trip from migratory salmon. ODFW identifies this park for both, but no park-specific best-month assessment was found; do not apply the above-Willamette-Falls coho outlook here.
planning.methods: For bass, ODFW describes jigs and prey-imitating lures around cover. Choose a presentation for the target species and check current lower-river rules; the linked health advisory is essential if keeping resident fish.

report.summary: No Cathedral Park-specific report found; latest narrative discusses upstream reaches.
report.coverage: Broader river; no dated St. Johns Bridge observation.

alerts.summary: Lower Willamette fish-consumption advisory applies here. OHA recommends not eating bass, carp or brown bullhead; review guidance for other resident fish.
Local bloom conditions are unverified. Check current notices; an absent advisory does not establish safety.

waters.name: Clackamas River
waters.description: A lower-river section served by two county parks.

planning.access_detail: Barton and Carver parks are public access anchors for this reach. Barton has bank access, a ramp and restrooms; Carver has a ramp near Clear Creek. A mapped park pair does not establish a safe float route or continuous public shoreline.

access_point.label: Carver Park boat ramp
access_point.map_query: Carver Park boat ramp Clackamas Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: ODFW identifies winter steelhead peaks around January and March, alongside summer-run fish. Autumn coho provide a separate target.
planning.methods: ODFW describes spinners, jigs, plugs and float presentations for coho; check gear rules.

report.summary: ODFW described good lower-river coho fishing.
report.coverage: Lower Clackamas; no Barton-to-Carver survey.

alerts.summary: Temporary park closures and river obstructions remain unverified; check notices before a float or bank trip.
Local bloom conditions are unverified. Check current notices; an absent advisory does not establish safety.

waters.name: Sandy River
waters.reach: Lewis and Clark State Recreation Site to mouth
waters.description: The lower Sandy near its Columbia River confluence.

planning.access_detail: ODFW identifies Lewis and Clark State Recreation Site for access toward the Sandy mouth, with a ramp, picnic area and restrooms. Stay within posted public access; current ramp usability and wading conditions are unverified.

access_point.label: Lewis and Clark State Recreation Site
access_point.map_query: Lewis and Clark State Recreation Site Sandy River Troutdale Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: ODFW identifies winter steelhead mainly December-April and summer-run fish May-August. These river-wide patterns are not opening dates or onsite observations.
planning.methods: Float a jig or swing a spinner for steelhead, subject to current lower Sandy gear and species rules.

report.summary: July report described summer-steelhead catches below the hatchery; no October update.
report.coverage: Below hatchery; no recent mouth-area observation.

alerts.summary: Local bloom conditions are unverified. Check current notices; an absent advisory does not establish safety.

waters.name: Wilson River
waters.description: A coastal river with migratory salmon, steelhead and resident trout fisheries.

planning.access_detail: ODFW lists bank access at Mills Bridge on Highway 6. Current parking, footing and neighboring land permissions are unverified.

access_point.label: Mills Bridge, Wilson River
access_point.map_query: Mills Bridge Wilson River Highway 6 Tillamook Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: Steelhead runs overlap; ODFW highlights spring/fall resident cutthroat and summer sea-run fish.
planning.methods: Work steelhead pools with spinners or floats; small spinners or flies suit cutthroat. Confirm seasonal gear rules.

report.summary: ODFW describes fall steelhead opportunity, with more fish upriver; Chinook remained concentrated nearer tidewater.
report.coverage: Wilson River overall; not a Mills Bridge catch or conditions survey.

alerts.summary: Local bloom conditions are unverified. Check current notices; an absent advisory does not establish safety.

waters.name: North Fork Nehalem River
waters.description: A popular steelhead destination centered on a small coastal stream and hatchery.

planning.access_detail: Hatchery bank access includes a platform for disabled-angling permit holders. Neighboring timberland permissions are unverified.

access_point.label: North Nehalem Fish Hatchery
access_point.map_query: North Nehalem Fish Hatchery Highway 53 Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: ODFW highlights December-January within a December-April window. This is a popular bank fishery.
planning.methods: ODFW suggests drift presentations, spinners or a float and jig; check hatchery deadlines and gear restrictions.

report.summary: Combined Nehalem report focuses on bay salmon and basin cutthroat; no current hatchery-area winter-steelhead assessment.
report.coverage: Combined Nehalem and North Fork report; bay salmon success is not evidence of fish at this hatchery reach.

alerts.summary: Hatchery access notices and local conditions are unverified. Check posted fishing boundaries and accessible-platform permit requirements.

waters.name: Siletz River
waters.description: A coastal river destination reached from Highway 229.

planning.access_detail: Jack Morgan Park at OR-229 mile 17.5 has a concrete ramp, vault toilets and picnic area west of the highway. Lincoln County directs access from the south through Siletz because the highway is blocked farther north.

access_point.label: A.W. Jack Morgan Park
access_point.map_query: A W Jack Morgan Park Siletz Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: Fall rain helps Chinook move upstream from tidewater. Steelhead provide a longer seasonal window; sea-run cutthroat arrive in summer and early fall.
planning.methods: Spinners or float presentations are established salmon approaches; small spinners or streamers suit cutthroat. Check current section-specific rules.

report.summary: ODFW reports salmon success in bay/tidewater and slow summer-steelhead fishing; conditions at Jack Morgan were not separately reported.
report.coverage: Siletz basin, with salmon observations downstream and steelhead discussion mainly upriver.

alerts.summary: OR-229 closed between mileposts 14-15 after a landslide. County says reach Jack Morgan Park from the south through Siletz; no local detour.
Local bloom conditions are unverified. Check current notices; an absent advisory does not establish safety.

sources.label: Lincoln County: Jack Morgan Park and road access

waters.name: Diamond Lake
waters.description: A Cascade trout lake with an established rainbow fishery and predator trout introduced for invasive-fish control.

planning.access_summary: North launch; Lake Creek shore options
planning.access_detail: The Marine Board lists the North Lake boat launch, and ODFW identifies shore fishing near Lake Creek. The destination is the public north launch; it is not a promise of accessible shoreline all around the north end.

access_point.label: Diamond Lake North End Boat Ramp
access_point.map_query: Diamond Lake North End Boat Ramp Oregon

planning.seasonal_summary: After ice-off and cooler autumn water
planning.seasonal_detail: ODFW background guidance highlights spring after ice-off and autumn cooling. Ice-off dates vary each year; this profile does not assess ice thickness or certify winter access.
planning.methods: ODFW describes trolling small lures and spinners, or fishing flies near Lake Creek. Shore and boat methods differ; no current north-end productive depth is recorded.

report.summary: ODFW reports good trout catches, with brown and tiger trout released.
report.coverage: Lake-wide report, not a north-shore catch survey.

alerts.summary: ODFW requires release of brown and tiger trout; review the full current species rules.
Oct 7 report says the main-ramp fish-cleaning station is under repair.
Present bloom status, snow and shoreline conditions are not established by this fishing report.

sources.label: ODFW Diamond Lake seasonal and method guide

waters.name: Detroit Lake
waters.description: A large Cascade reservoir east of Salem, with coldwater lake fisheries.

planning.access_detail: Mongold Day-use Area has a public ramp, trailer parking, restrooms and picnic facilities. Falling reservoir levels change shoreline access and launch usability; use the current operator notice before towing.

access_point.label: Mongold Day-use Area
access_point.map_query: Mongold Day Use Area Detroit Lake Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: Cooler surface water favors rainbow fishing. Kokanee tend to move deeper as summer advances; lake-wide patterns do not establish fish depth at Mongold today.
planning.methods: Try standard trout presentations from bank or boat. For kokanee, ODFW describes trolling small spinners behind flashers or jigging; depth control matters.

report.summary: Trout remained active; Mongold was the remaining usable ramp in this dated report.
report.coverage: Lake-wide fishing; Mongold ramp update, not live level.

alerts.summary: Other ramps were out of water on Sept. 28. Recheck Mongold before towing.
Local bloom conditions are unverified. Check current notices; an absent advisory does not establish safety.

waters.name: Henry Hagg Lake
waters.description: A Coast Range foothill reservoir combining trout and warmwater fishing.

planning.access_detail: Scoggins Valley Park provides shore access, two launches, an accessible fishing pier and restrooms. The public C-Ramp recreation area is one named arrival point; check current park hours and ramp notices.

access_point.label: Hagg Lake C-Ramp Recreation Area
access_point.map_query: Henry Hagg Lake C Ramp Recreation Area Gaston Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: Early-season bank trout and warmer-water bass offer different trips. Bass use shallow arms as water warms; reservoir drawdown changes available cover.
planning.methods: ODFW suggests spinners for bank trout and soft plastics, grubs or jigs for bass. Work submerged structure and adjust to water level.

report.summary: ODFW described active fall bass around submerged structure; recheck park conditions.
report.coverage: Lake-wide; no C-Ramp survey or measured temperature.

alerts.summary: OHA statewide mercury advisory applies to bass. Review species-specific consumption guidance before keeping fish.
Local bloom conditions are unverified. Check current notices; an absent advisory does not establish safety.

waters.name: Odell Lake
waters.description: A large natural lake beside Highway 58, known for kokanee and lake trout.

planning.access_summary: Princess Creek: public ramp and campground
planning.access_detail: Recreation.gov identifies Princess Creek Campground and its Odell Lake boat ramp. ODFW names the adjacent north shore as a kokanee starting area. Check day-use access and launch conditions independently of a camping reservation.

access_point.label: Princess Creek Campground and Boat Ramp
access_point.map_query: Princess Creek Campground Boat Ramp Odell Lake Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: ODFW guide timing favors spring and fall for kokanee and lake trout. Seasonal habitat patterns are separate from the approaching angling closure.
planning.methods: Troll or jig for kokanee at the depth of marked schools. Boat access improves reach; do not assign a depth without present observations.

report.summary: ODFW reports small kokanee and productive lake-trout fishing.
report.coverage: Odell Lake overall; Princess Creek is not separately sampled.

alerts.summary: ODFW reports angling closes Nov 1, 2026; bull trout must be released.
Current wind, waves, bloom status and launch usability need a trip-day check.

waters.name: Wallowa Lake
waters.reach: South end at Wallowa Lake State Park
waters.description: A natural lake at the foot of the Wallowa Mountains with kokanee and trout fisheries.

planning.access_detail: Wallowa Lake State Park provides south-end shore access, a boat launch, picnic areas and restrooms. Marina rentals and services are seasonal; the park notes service changes from October into May.

access_point.label: Wallowa Lake State Park boat launch
access_point.map_query: Wallowa Lake State Park boat launch Joseph Oregon

planning.seasonal_detail: Kokanee are generally shallower in May-early July and move deeper later. Stocked rainbows offer a shore option at the south end; spawning fish in the inlet are separate from the lake fishery.
planning.methods: Cast spinners or fish a float presentation for nearshore rainbows. Troll a small spinner or jig for kokanee, adjusting depth to observed fish rather than assuming a fixed depth.

report.summary: ODFW described south-end nearshore trout and deeper kokanee, generally below 45 feet; inlet kokanee spawning had begun.
report.coverage: Lake-wide report with south-end trout guidance; reported kokanee depth is dated angling information, not a live measurement.

alerts.summary: Marina services are seasonal; current facilities and temporary closures remain unverified. Check the park before relying on rentals or facilities.
Local bloom conditions are unverified. Check current notices; an absent advisory does not establish safety.

waters.name: Cowlitz River
waters.description: The big lower river running through Kelso, fed by Toutle River water above Castle Rock.

planning.access_detail: A local launch guide places the Gearhart Gardens ramp just off I-5 exit 36: cross the Cowlitz River bridge, then turn right onto Gearhart Garden Road and use the northern lot; the first lot holds an old, abandoned ramp. Much of the river runs past private property, so stay on public ground. This is a launch description, not a WDFW site inspection.

access_point.label: Gearhart Gardens boat ramp, Kelso
access_point.map_query: Gearhart Gardens boat launch Cowlitz River Kelso WA

access_points.label: Gearhart Gardens boat ramp
access_points.note: Off I-5 exit 36 in Kelso. Use the northern lot.
access_points.map_query: Gearhart Gardens boat launch Cowlitz River Kelso WA

planning.seasonal_summary: Fall coho now; Chinook reported release-only
planning.seasonal_detail: October creel checks show hatchery coho and some steelhead on the lower river. A local shop report lists hatchery steelhead, hatchery sea-run cutthroat and hatchery coho as open with no Chinook retention. Winter steelhead are a separate planning window; confirm the rules for your dates.
planning.methods: Creel checks record both bank and boat anglers on the lower river. Choose gear after checking WDFW anti-snagging and hook rules for this section.

report.summary: Bank anglers below the I-5 bridge kept three coho; above it, two steelhead.
report.coverage: WDFW creel checks Oct 5-11, summarized by Northwest Sportsman. The below-I-5 section starts at the bridge near Toledo and includes, but is broader than, Kelso to Castle Rock.

alerts.summary: A Kelso shop report dated Oct 6, 2026 says Chinook may not be retained on the Cowlitz this fall. Confirm current species and limit rules with WDFW.

Washington tributaries need a Washington fishing license; Oregon reciprocity covers shared Columbia River boundary waters, not these rivers. A 2026 rules summary lists a new Columbia River Salmon and Steelhead Endorsement for anglers 15 and older.
WDFW water access sites need a Discover Pass or a Vehicle Access Pass. Check which pass applies to the launch you use.

waters.name: Cowlitz River
waters.description: The famous hatchery stretch below the Barrier Dam near Salkum, about 45 minutes north of Kelso.

planning.access_summary: Blue Creek and Barrier Dam: bank, launch, ADA spots
planning.access_detail: Lewis County's guide places Blue Creek next to the salmon hatchery off Spencer Road, about three miles east of Jackson Highway, with restrooms and a fishing spot for anglers in wheelchairs. A local angling guide routes it from I-5 east on Highway 12, right on Fuller Road in Salkum, left on Spencer Road, then right at the fork to the hatchery and dam. The Barrier Dam access is a little over a mile south of Salkum off Fuller Road, with paved parking, restrooms and an ADA fishing ramp. Blue Creek's launch is listed as a Tacoma Power site.

access_points.label: Barrier Dam
access_points.note: South of Salkum off Fuller Road. Busy during salmon runs; closed water starts near the dam.

planning.seasonal_summary: Fall coho now; winter steelhead arriving soon
planning.seasonal_detail: A Kelso shop report dated Oct 6 says coho are in at Blue Creek and fishing is good, the summer steelhead run is about over and winter steelhead will arrive soon. Spring Chinook bring the biggest crowds to the Barrier Dam. No fish are counted at Blue Creek itself; Tacoma Power's hatchery separator counts are the nearest run data.
planning.methods: Bank anglers line both access points. Past WDFW rules set an anti-snagging rule and a night closure from April through November here; confirm current gear rules before fishing.

report.summary: Coho are in at Blue Creek and fishing is good.
report.coverage: Sportsman's Warehouse Kelso report for Blue Creek. A shop report, not a WDFW creel survey.

alerts.summary: Closed waters apply near the Barrier Dam and the hatchery, and past rules banned fishing from the south bank from May 1 to June 15. Check the posted boundaries and current dates.
Past WDFW rules here included an anti-snagging rule and a night closure from April 1 through November 30. Confirm they still apply.
A Kelso shop report says Chinook may not be retained on the Cowlitz this fall. Confirm species and limits with WDFW.

waters.name: Coweeman River
waters.description: A small Kelso tributary of the Cowlitz with fall Chinook, coho and winter steelhead.

planning.access_detail: No documented public fishing access point was verified for the lower river. The Coweeman River Trail in Kelso has no designated parking and is not established as a fishing entrance. WDFW lists a weir on the Coweeman this season.
planning.seasonal_summary: Reported closed through Oct 31 for spawning Chinook
planning.seasonal_detail: Basin planning documents describe fall Chinook, coho and winter steelhead runs, with the middle and upper river most important for steelhead. In past seasons the river reopened to hatchery steelhead and hatchery salmon on November 1; confirm this season's opener.
planning.methods: A fishing method is not established while the river is reported closed. Check the reopening rules, then confirm a legal public access point.

report.summary: A Kelso shop listing says the river is closed Sep 1 to Oct 31 to protect spawning Chinook.
report.coverage: Shop report for the whole river; not a WDFW notice or an on-site check.

alerts.summary: Reported closed Sep 1 to Oct 31, 2026 to protect spawning Chinook. Confirm the closure and the reopening date with WDFW.

planning.score_notice: A local report lists the Coweeman as closed through October 31 to protect spawning Chinook; the fishing score is withheld until the rules are confirmed.

waters.name: Toutle River
waters.description: The Mount St. Helens river that joins the Cowlitz above Castle Rock, with hatchery fish from the Toutle program.

planning.access_detail: No WDFW fishing access site was verified on this reach. Paddling guides describe put-ins between the SR 504 bridge and Tower Road; a paddling put-in is not established as legal bank-fishing access. WDFW lists a weir on the South Fork Toutle this season.
planning.seasonal_summary: Hatchery coho in fall; hatchery steelhead in tributaries
planning.seasonal_detail: Past WDFW notices describe hatchery coho fisheries on the North Fork near the fish collection facility, and hatchery summer steelhead released into the South Fork Toutle and Green rivers. Those notices are from earlier seasons; this year's boundaries and dates need a check.
planning.methods: Past WDFW notices required hatchery-only retention with wild steelhead released, and selective gear during early steelhead openers. Confirm current gear rules before fishing.

report.summary: A Kelso shop rates the Toutle as fair and lists it open for hatchery steelhead, hatchery coho, and trout (2 a day over 14 inches).
report.coverage: Sportsman's Warehouse Kelso report for the Toutle; not a WDFW creel survey or a specific reach.

alerts.summary: Seasons, boundaries and limits for the mainstem, North Fork, South Fork and Green River differ and were not confirmed for 2026.
In past seasons WDFW kept the North Fork hatchery facility closed to the public and directed anglers to signed trails around it.

waters.name: Lewis River
waters.description: The busiest fall river in the area this week, with several public launches east of Woodland.

planning.access_summary: Pekin Ferry and Island launches; bank
planning.access_detail: WDFW lists Pekin Ferry as a concrete ramp with restrooms, open year-round, with bank fishing and boat access, reached from I-5 exit 21 via SR 503 and South Pekin Road. waters.name: Elochoman River
waters.description: A small coastal-feeling river at Cathlamet, west of Longview, mostly fished below the hatchery.

planning.access_summary: Some bank spots; public route unverified
planning.access_detail: A fishing guide describes fair access, mostly by drift boat, with some bank spots below Beaver Creek Hatchery and private property along the river. WDFW has proposed buying land west of the hatchery for public access; that purchase is not confirmed here. WDFW's report warns boaters about an old weir sill near the hatchery.
planning.seasonal_summary: Coho in Oct-Nov; winter steelhead Dec-Jan
planning.seasonal_detail: Guides describe October and November as the best salmon months, a winter steelhead run from December through March that peaks in December and January, and a summer run from June to September. Most steelhead caught are hatchery fish; wild fish must be released.
planning.methods: Most anglers drift the river. Hatchery steelhead have the adipose fin removed, which is how kept fish are identified. Check current gear rules.

report.summary: No dated 2026 catch report specific to the Elochoman was found.
report.coverage: WDFW's southwest report carries a boating caution near the hatchery; it is not a catch survey.

alerts.summary: In 2023 WDFW closed salmon fishing below the Beaver Creek Road Bridge in November to protect hatchery broodstock. Check for a similar closure this season.
